learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the inner drives that push us to act, and the complex feelings that color all of our psychological experiences!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Motivation is an internal state that energizes and directs behavior. The cycle goes: Need (deprivation) -> Drive (tension) -> Arousal -> Goal-directed behavior -> Achievement -> Reduction of arousal.
Biological motives (hunger, thirst, sleep) are innate and needed for survival. Psychosocial motives (need for achievement, affiliation, power) are learned through social interaction.

Abraham Maslow proposed that motives are arranged in a pyramid. We must satisfy lower basic needs (physiological, safety) before we can pursue higher psychological needs, peaking at 'Self-Actualization'.
Emotions are complex patterns involving three components: Physiological arousal (heart beating fast), Subjective feeling (feeling afraid), and Behavioral expression (running away or screaming).
High anxiety and anger impair performance and health. Managing emotions involves enhancing self-awareness, cognitive reappraisal (changing how you think about a situation), and relaxation techniques.

fun_activity.title: 🎭 Emotion Charades
fun_activity.instructions: Can you convey an emotion using only your facial expressions? Stand in front of a mirror (or a friend) and try to express 'disgust', 'surprise', and 'contempt' without making a sound or using your hands. Paul Ekman found these expressions are universal!

exam_tips: 📌 Always draw the pyramid diagram when answering a question on Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs.
📌 Be able to distinguish between 'Need' (biological lack) and 'Drive' (the psychological tension it causes).
📌 The 'Need for Achievement' (n-Ach) is a frequent question regarding psychosocial motives.
quick_recap: ⭐ The hypothalamus plays a crucial role in regulating basic biological motives like hunger and thirst.
⭐ Frustration occurs when the path to a goal is blocked.
⭐ Emotional intelligence (EQ) is the ability to monitor one's own and others' emotions and use this to guide thinking and actions.
